tasks.short: Talk with colleagues about students' support each day, share support arrangements, take part in team meetings about students, and note agreements in the student files.

steps.what: Special education teacher collaborates with other teachers about students' support
Special education teacher e-mails support tips and arrangements to colleagues
Special education teacher takes part in team meetings to ensure students receive appropriate support
Special education teacher notes agreements in the student files

tasks.design: Each student has a short support card in the pupil record system ({OTHER}) with the arrangements that work, visible to every teacher of that student, so tips are not e-mailed again each term. Agreements from team meetings go on the same card. Talking with colleagues and team meetings stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support tips went by e-mail and got lost between terms.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil record systems can show notes to all teachers of a student.
tasks.still_hard: Busy teachers do not always read the card.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a subject teacher that a small change will help a student.

reach.learn: Whether support arrangements are known from the first lesson.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records and learning-goal tracking shared among staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from student needs to agreements noted; lessons are outside.
Input contract: support cards kept in the pupil record system; fallback is e-mail.
Talks and meetings do not change.
Colleagues read the card in about the time they read an e-mail.
research_questions: Do subject teachers apply the arrangements more often?

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps support cards current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few students with support; high: many students taught by many teachers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe lessons by teachers and assistants, check that support arrangements are applied, give feedback, and note observations.

steps.what: Special education teacher observes lessons to monitor teachers and teacher assistants
Special education teacher checks records to see that inclusive program requirements are applied
Special education teacher gives feedback to teachers and assistants
Special education teacher notes observations on paper

tasks.design: The pupil record system ({OTHER}) shows per student which support arrangements are in the plan and whether they were logged, so the teacher sees gaps without leafing through files. Observations go on a tablet form linked to the program requirements. Observing and giving feedback stay with the teacher. The overview is per student, not a score per staff member, and needs staff consent under the school participation rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans and logs were read file by file and observations noted on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil record systems show plan arrangements per student.
tasks.still_hard: Feedback to colleagues can strain working relations.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching an assistant without undermining them in front of students.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records with a development plan module and learning-goal tracking.
Under the WMS, staff consent to tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the observation plan to observation notes; formal staff appraisals are outside.
Input contract: plans and logs in the pupil record system; fallback is files and paper.
Observing and feedback do not change.
Staff consent comes before the overview is used.
research_questions: Are arrangements applied more often after feedback?

incremental.description: Special education teacher explains the overview to staff.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small team; high: many teachers and assistants.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange the parent meeting, have parents pick a slot, prepare the progress overview, meet parents to discuss progress and determine priorities and resource needs, write the agreements, send them to parents, and request resources.

steps.what: Special education teacher arranges the parent meeting by phone and e-mail
Special education teacher prepares the progress overview for the meeting
Special education teacher meets parents to discuss their children's progress and determine priorities
Special education teacher writes the agreements
Special education teacher e-mails the agreements to the parents
Special education teacher requests resources the child needs from the care coordinator

tasks.design: Parents pick a meeting slot in the school's parent app, so times are not agreed by phone. The pupil record system ({OTHER}) gives a progress overview per student for the meeting. Agreements are noted in a short form and, once written, go to the parents through the parent app. Resource needs go to the care coordinator on a request form ({WORKFLOW}). The talk with parents and setting priorities stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times were agreed by phone and overviews built from several files.
tasks.enabler_now: Parent apps take slot bookings; pupil record systems show progress overviews.
tasks.still_hard: Some parents do not use the app and need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a parent fears behind a question about grades.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records and learning-goal tracking, with the Parro parent app.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting due to the resource request; the resources themselves are outside.
Input contract: progress in the pupil record system; fallback is phone and files.
Parents pick a slot in the app in about the time a call took; a little parent time is priced.
The talk with parents does not change.
research_questions: Do agreements reach parents the same day more often?

incremental.description: Special education teacher calls parents who do not use the app.
Parents book a slot in the app.

approvals.approved_version: The agreements as written by the teacher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few parents use the app; high: most parents book in the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct students in the use and care of equipment, monitor them during use, check equipment for damage and report defects, and keep the picture instruction cards.

steps.what: Special education teacher instructs students in the use and care of equipment and materials
Special education teacher monitors students during use to prevent injuries and damage
Special education teacher checks equipment for damage and reports defects
Special education teacher keeps the picture instruction cards for equipment

tasks.design: A QR code on each piece of equipment opens a defect form for the facilities desk ({HELPDESK}), so defects are reported in one scan instead of a note or a walk to the office. Picture instruction cards are shared in the school's document space ({DOCS}) instead of each teacher making their own. Instructing and watching students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defects were reported on notes or in person and each teacher made own cards.
tasks.enabler_now: QR defect forms and shared document spaces are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Students with disabilities need instructions repeated and adapted.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a student about to misuse a tool and stepping in calmly.

evidence.claim: QR codes can open defect forms; shared document spaces hold instruction cards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lesson with equipment to defects reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: facilities desk handles defect forms; fallback is notes.
Instructing and monitoring do not change.
research_questions: Are defective items taken out of use sooner?

incremental.description: Special education teacher adds new cards to the shared space.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: little equipment; high: workshop lessons with much equipment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps working with colleagues, coaching staff, talking with parents and keeping students safe; e-mailed tips, paper notes and phone rounds shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time in class and with parents.
